claims.text: Separately computing lattice and electronic heat transport using first-principles techniques will produce roughly 20% lower prediction error than models that conflate the two contributions.
The intended samples are well-homogenized HfNbTaTiZr bulk crystals that are either defect-free or contain controlled low-level oxygen.
The proposed multiscale approach independently models phonon and electron contributions using DFT-derived elastic properties and electronic-structure calculations.
Lattice and electronic thermal-conductivity contributions in HfNbTaTiZr are comparable below 200 K.
Measured total thermal conductivity of HfNbTaTiZr is approximately 10–17 W/(K m) from 300 to 1200 K.
Temperature-dependent force constants and adjusted Debye-like parameters can be used to evaluate the alloy's phonon dispersion.
Electronic-structure calculations can capture the scattering rates and density of states needed to evaluate electronic heat transport.
Separate phonon and electronic calculations decouple the two energy-transport pathways.
Decoupling the transport channels permits individual calibration of the phonon and electron contributions against experimental baselines.
Individual calibration of the two channels reduces inaccuracies associated with unified analytical models.
The proposed model will predict total thermal conductivity within approximately 20% of experiment.
The proposed model will accurately resolve comparable lattice and electronic contributions at low temperatures.
The proposed model will predict the appropriate magnitude of total thermal conductivity at high temperatures.
Earlier predictive approaches combined lattice and electronic contributions through unified or effective-medium approximations.
Earlier approaches had errors exceeding 30% relative to temperature-dependent experimental measurements.
The model is applicable to well-prepared HfNbTaTiZr with or without low-level oxygen over temperatures where both phonon and electronic transport are active.
Defect-heavy or compositionally altered HfNbTaTiZr may require model recalibration.
The model's improvement may vary with sample quality and measurement uncertainty.
Time-domain thermal reflectance can be used to probe phonon-dominated transport in these samples.
Electrical measurements combined with the Wiedemann–Franz law can estimate the electronic thermal-conductivity contribution.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis alternates among a 20% relative reduction in error, prediction within a 20% absolute error margin, and an approximately 20% improvement. These are different performance metrics and are not reconciled.

The predicted outcome promises agreement within about 20%, but the model is only declared falsified when error exceeds about 30%. Errors between 20% and 30% would violate the prediction without satisfying the stated falsification rule.
